passages.title: Candy Village Summer Fair
passages.text: Candy Village Summer Fair — Saturday 14th July, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., in the village square. Cake competition at 2 p.m.: please bring your cake to the bakery by 12 o'clock. Face painting for children: £2. Entry is free! If it rains, the fair will move to the school hall.

questions.q: Where must you take your cake before the competition?
questions.explain: 'Please bring your cake to the bakery by 12 o'clock.'

questions.q: What do you have to pay for?
questions.explain: Face painting costs £2; entry is free.

questions.q: What happens if it rains?
options: The fair moves to the school hall.
The fair moves to next Saturday.
questions.explain: 'If it rains, the fair will move to the school hall.'

passages.title: An Email from Ella
passages.text: Hi Leo, Thanks for inviting me to your birthday party on Friday. I'd love to come, but I have a piano lesson until five. Can I arrive at about half past five? Also, my brother wants to know if he can come too. He doesn't know many people here because we only moved last month. See you soon, Ella

questions.q: Why will Ella be late?
questions.explain: 'I have a piano lesson until five.'

questions.q: What does Ella ask Leo?
questions.explain: 'My brother wants to know if he can come too.'

questions.q: What do we learn about Ella's family?
options: Her brother is older than her.

passages.title: The Gingerbread Baker
passages.text: Mr Crumb opened his bakery forty years ago. At first he only sold bread, but one winter he made gingerbread houses for the village children. They were so popular that people came from other towns to buy them. Now his granddaughter Poppy helps him. She decorates the houses with sweets while Mr Crumb bakes. He says he will never stop working because he loves seeing children smile.

questions.q: What did the bakery sell at first?
Who decorates the gingerbread houses?
Why won't Mr Crumb stop working?

passages.title: Camping by the River
passages.text: Last weekend my family went camping by the river. On Saturday we went fishing, but we didn't catch anything! In the evening it got very cold, so we made a fire and cooked sausages. On Sunday morning it rained heavily and our tent got wet. We packed up early and drove home, but we all agreed it was a great adventure.

questions.q: How many fish did they catch?
Why did they make a fire?
questions.explain: 'It got very cold, so we made a fire.'

questions.q: What happened on Sunday?
options: It rained and the tent got wet.
questions.explain: 'It rained heavily and our tent got wet.'

passages.title: Lost Kitten!
passages.text: LOST: small grey kitten wearing a blue collar with a bell. Last seen near the library on Tuesday evening. She is very shy and may hide under cars. Please call Jack on 07700 900123. Reward!

questions.q: What colour is the kitten's collar?
questions.explain: '…wearing a blue collar with a bell.'

questions.q: Where was the kitten last seen?
What is the kitten like?

passages.title: The Sweet Shop Job
passages.text: Hi Ollie, guess what? I've got a Saturday job at Mrs Plum's sweet shop! I start at nine and finish at three. I help customers, put sweets into jars and clean the counter. The pay isn't great, but Mrs Plum lets me take home any broken lollipops! Last Saturday it was really busy because of the village fair. Are you free next Sunday? We could go to the lake. Love, Kit

questions.q: How long does Kit work on Saturdays?
questions.explain: From nine to three = six hours.

questions.q: What does Kit like about the job?
questions.explain: 'Mrs Plum lets me take home any broken lollipops!'

questions.q: Why was the shop busy last Saturday?

passages.title: Ride the Candy Train
passages.text: The Candy Train goes around Candy Village every hour from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. The trip takes 40 minutes. Tickets cost £4 for adults and £2 for children. Children under three travel free. You can buy tickets at the station or on the train, but it's cheaper online. Dogs are welcome, but please keep them on a lead.

questions.q: How long is one trip?
Where are tickets cheapest?
What must dog owners do?
options: keep their dog on a lead
buy their dog a child's ticket
leave their dog at the station
sit at the back of the train
